E1.evidence:
Issue #22: "The following commit fixed an issue with isnan for kinetic: https://github.com/yujinrobot/kobuki_core/commit/2d943e14e99d6d645729b97c5f6dcb10d415f8ff
Could we have that fix backported to indigo as well?"; the maintainer confirms and applies it: "Cherried in b166c939.

Coming soon to indigo in v0.6.4." The concrete defect is the unqualified call `if (isnan(heading_offset) == true)` in kobuki_driver/src/driver/kobuki.cpp. No reproducer or error log is given.

E2.evidence: kobuki_driver calls an unqualified isnan that it obtains transitively (kobuki.cpp at 0.6.3 includes no math header itself; ecl/math.hpp -> ecl/math/fuzzy.hpp includes <cmath>, and the same ecl_core branch release/0.61-indigo-kinetic serves both distros). The fix makes the consumer include <cmath> and call std::isnan, i.e. it changes which provider API element the consumer references. Whether the unqualified name is available depends on the standard-library/C-library headers the consumer is compiled against, so the defect depends on an assumption between kobuki_driver and those headers and is not internal to one unit; the resolving change is source code, not a build-system, packaging, or name-binding change.

E3.evidence: UPGRADE: the fix was made "for kinetic", i.e. for the newer distro's toolchain, against code that had been used with earlier toolchains; the issue asks for the same change on the indigo branch. The toolchain versions are not named.

E4.evidence: Only a code-level statement of the mismatch: the maintainer's commit "[kobuki_driver] isnan -> std::isnan" and the dataset record ("a macro was being used instead of the proper function call to determine whether a value is NaN"). No observed failure is documented, so the outcome is undocumented.

units.name: C++ toolchain math headers
units.revision_basis: The sources say only that the change fixed "an issue with isnan for kinetic"; no compiler, libstdc++, or glibc version is named, so the provider is described by a label for the (unspecified) Kinetic-era toolchain referred to in issue #22 (2016-06-17). The resolution does not change the provider.

units.name: kobuki_driver
units.revision_basis: Broken: 0.6.3 (57b89147) is the parent of the indigo cherry-pick b166c93 and the indigo release current when the issue was filed; kobuki.cpp line 276 there reads `if (isnan(heading_offset) == true)`. Resolved: b166c93 (committed 2016-06-17, released in 0.6.4 per the maintainer), which adds #include <cmath> and calls std::isnan.

loudness_evidence: No diagnostic or observed failure appears in the issue or either commit; the issue says only "fixed an issue with isnan for kinetic".

resolution.summary: kobuki_driver includes <cmath> and calls std::isnan(heading_offset) instead of the unqualified isnan (kinetic commit 2d943e14, cherry-picked to indigo as b166c93).

notes: The sources never state the failure mode or the toolchain; the provider unit is therefore named generically and has no quoted artifact (empty section in the artifact file), and consumer_built_against for the broken composition is null because no earlier provider revision is documented or recoverable.
